paragraphs.source_en: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of Keichō 5, Tokugawa Ieyasu, supreme commander of the Eastern Army, began operations at daybreak and won the Battle of Sekigahara at the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Monkey, two and a half hours later than planned.

units.source_en: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of Keichō 5, Tokugawa Ieyasu, supreme commander of the Eastern Army, began operations at daybreak and won the Battle of Sekigahara at the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Monkey, two and a half hours later than planned.
units.source_zh: 庆长五年九月十五，从黎明时分发起行动的东军总帅德川家康，比预定计划晚两个半时辰，于申时四刻获得了关原合战的胜利。

paragraphs.source_zh: 庆长五年九月十五，从黎明时分发起行动的东军总帅德川家康，比预定计划晚两个半时辰，于申时四刻获得了关原合战的胜利。

paragraphs.source_en: After moving his headquarters to Fujikawadai, Ieyasu no longer bit his nails. Until noon, the great encampment at Fujikawadai had been Ōtani Yoshitsugu’s position. Yoshitsugu was gone. Nor was Yoshitsugu alone: Shimazu Toyohisa, whose valor was unsurpassed beneath heaven, was also gone, while Shima Sakon Katsutake, called Ishida Mitsunari’s right-hand man, had vanished without a trace.

units.source_en: After moving his headquarters to Fujikawadai, Ieyasu no longer bit his nails.
units.source_zh: 移阵藤川台之后的家康，已不再啃咬指甲了。

units.source_en: Until noon, the great encampment at Fujikawadai had been Ōtani Yoshitsugu’s position.
units.source_zh: 藤川台的这座大营，中午之前还是大谷吉继的阵地。

units.source_en: Yoshitsugu was gone.

units.source_en: Nor was Yoshitsugu alone: Shimazu Toyohisa, whose valor was unsurpassed beneath heaven, was also gone, while Shima Sakon Katsutake, called Ishida Mitsunari’s right-hand man, had vanished without a trace.

paragraphs.source_zh: 移阵藤川台之后的家康，已不再啃咬指甲了。藤川台的这座大营，中午之前还是大谷吉继的阵地。吉继人已不在。不仅吉继，勇冠天下的岛津丰久也不在了，被称为石田三成左膀右臂的岛左近胜猛，亦不知所终。

paragraphs.source_en: Though no definite news had arrived, Ishida Mitsunari, Konishi Yukinaga, Ukita Hideie, and Natsuka Masaie alike must now be trudging despondently along mountain paths, exposed to wind and rain.

units.source_en: Though no definite news had arrived, Ishida Mitsunari, Konishi Yukinaga, Ukita Hideie, and Natsuka Masaie alike must now be trudging despondently along mountain paths, exposed to wind and rain.
units.source_zh: 虽无准确消息传来，但无论是石田三成、小西行长、宇喜多秀家，还是长束正家，此刻定都心灰意冷走在山路上，任风吹雨打。

paragraphs.source_zh: 虽无准确消息传来，但无论是石田三成、小西行长、宇喜多秀家，还是长束正家，此刻定都心灰意冷走在山路上，任风吹雨打。

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsunari’s chief retainer Gamō Bitchū-no-kami had fallen together with his sons Daizen and Ōinosuke. Okudaira Sadaharu, the envoy sent to Kobayakawa’s position, had perished in the melee with Ōtani’s troops. Tōdō Takatora’s cousin Genba had been killed. Oda Urakusai was wounded. Ii Naomasa was wounded. Matsudaira Shimotsuke-no-kami was wounded...

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成的家老蒲生备中守与其子大膳、大炊助一同战死。被派到小早川阵地的使者奥平贞治，在与大谷部的混战中殉身。藤堂高虎的堂弟玄蕃战死。织田有乐斋负伤。井伊直政负伤。松平下野守负伤……

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu listened to these reports without expression and nodded. For a commander, it was enough that the situation as a whole was secure.

units.source_en: For a commander, it was enough that the situation as a whole was secure.
units.source_zh: 作为统帅，大局稳定即可。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康面无表情听完这些报告，点了点头。作为统帅，大局稳定即可。

paragraphs.source_en: The first vanguard commander to return from the battlefield was Kuroda Nagamasa. A finger on Nagamasa’s left hand was broken, and he had roughly wrapped it in a strip of cloth now soaked with blood. He had removed his helmet and hung it from his shoulder; his disheveled hair was caked with mud. Ieyasu praised Nagamasa lavishly and presented him with the Yoshimitsu dagger.

units.source_en: The first vanguard commander to return from the battlefield was Kuroda Nagamasa.
units.source_zh: 从战场上最先赶回的前锋大将乃黑田长政。

units.source_en: A finger on Nagamasa’s left hand was broken, and he had roughly wrapped it in a strip of cloth now soaked with blood.

units.source_zh: 家康盛赞了长政一番，取来短刀吉光赏给他。

paragraphs.source_zh: 从战场上最先赶回的前锋大将乃黑田长政。长政左手一指骨折，用一块布胡乱缠了几下，布上渗满血。他把头盔摘下来挂在肩上，杂乱的头发上沾满泥巴。家康盛赞了长政一番，取来短刀吉光赏给他。

paragraphs.source_en: Only then did Ieyasu finally breathe a deep sigh of relief.

units.source_en: Only then did Ieyasu finally breathe a deep sigh of relief.
units.source_zh: 直到此时，家康方大大松了口气。

paragraphs.source_zh: 直到此时，家康方大大松了口气。

paragraphs.source_en: “Let us acclaim our victory!”

units.source_en: “Let us acclaim our victory!”

paragraphs.source_zh: “欢呼胜利！”

paragraphs.source_en: “Very well. The enemy below Mount Nangū has collapsed, and not one enemy remains in sight upon the field. We have destroyed nearly thirty thousand of the enemy and captured some fifteen or sixteen hundred warhorses... This is a victory without precedent.”

units.source_en: “Very well.
The enemy below Mount Nangū has collapsed, and not one enemy remains in sight upon the field.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu, however, silently removed the brown crêpe-silk headcloth from his head. “Bring me my helmet. The one with the white lining.” Seeing Ieyasu put his helmet on once more, the men exchanged bewildered glances.

units.source_en: Ieyasu, however, silently removed the brown crêpe-silk headcloth from his head.

paragraphs.source_en: “The true battle is only now beginning. As for acclaiming victory, I think we should wait until we reach Ōsaka. We may celebrate once every hostage being held there has been rescued safely. Fasten my helmet cords!”

units.source_zh: “真正的仗现在才刚刚开始。

units.source_en: As for acclaiming victory, I think we should wait until we reach Ōsaka.

units.source_en: Fasten my helmet cords!”

paragraphs.source_zh: “真正的仗现在才刚刚开始。要欢呼胜利，我看还是等到了大坂之后再说吧。等我们把被扣的人质全部平安解救出来，再庆祝胜利不迟。把头盔带子给我系好！”

paragraphs.source_en: Those few words touched everyone present, and some began to shed tears. The men had fought on the battlefield with the courage and hardness of iron; Ieyasu’s words passed through their stout hearts like a warm spring breeze.

units.source_en: Those few words touched everyone present, and some began to shed tears.
units.source_zh: 一句话打动了在场的每一个人，有人竟簌簌落下泪来。

units.source_en: The men had fought on the battlefield with the courage and hardness of iron; Ieyasu’s words passed through their stout hearts like a warm spring breeze.
units.source_zh: 众人在战场上英勇奋战，皆如铁人，家康的话有如一阵温暖的春风，拂过这些铁骨铮铮的汉子心头。

paragraphs.source_zh: 一句话打动了在场的每一个人，有人竟簌簌落下泪来。众人在战场上英勇奋战，皆如铁人，家康的话有如一阵温暖的春风，拂过这些铁骨铮铮的汉子心头。

paragraphs.source_en: “Forgive my foolishness.”

units.source_en: “Forgive my foolishness.”
units.source_zh: “请恕在下愚鲁。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “请恕在下愚鲁。”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes, the war is far from over.”

units.source_en: “Yes, the war is far from over.”
units.source_zh: “是啊，战事还远未结束。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “是啊，战事还远未结束。”

paragraphs.source_en: “Indeed. The generals’ hostages are all still confined in Ōsaka. Tomorrow we shall march for Sawayama without delay.”

units.source_en: “Indeed. The generals’ hostages are all still confined in Ōsaka.
units.source_zh: “是，诸将人质都还关押在大坂。

units.source_en: Tomorrow we shall march for Sawayama without delay.”
units.source_zh: 明日我们便立刻向佐和山进发。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “是，诸将人质都还关押在大坂。明日我们便立刻向佐和山进发。”

paragraphs.source_en: Even in victory, one must tighten the cords of one’s helmet. Those heartening words were both a warning and a balm to soothe the spirit. At so delicate a moment, Ieyasu’s words contained the secret—and the painstaking care—by which he would bring peace to the realm.

units.source_en: Even in victory, one must tighten the cords of one’s helmet.
units.source_zh: 尽管胜利了，但依然要系紧头盔带子。

units.source_en: Those heartening words were both a warning and a balm to soothe the spirit.

units.source_en: At so delicate a moment, Ieyasu’s words contained the secret—and the painstaking care—by which he would bring peace to the realm.
units.source_zh: 在如此微妙的时刻，家康的话里蕴含了安抚天下的秘诀和苦心。

paragraphs.source_zh: 尽管胜利了，但依然要系紧头盔带子。一句鼓舞人心的话，既是警告，又是抚慰人心的良药。在如此微妙的时刻，家康的话里蕴含了安抚天下的秘诀和苦心。

paragraphs.source_en: Honda Tadakatsu quietly wiped away his tears and called loudly, “Lord Fukushima Masanori has arrived.”

units.source_en: Honda Tadakatsu quietly wiped away his tears and called loudly, “Lord Fukushima Masanori has arrived.”

paragraphs.source_zh: 本多忠胜悄悄擦了把泪，高声道：“福岛正则大人到。”

paragraphs.source_en: Tadakatsu was perhaps the elder of the Tokugawa house who best understood the ways of the human heart. Once Tadakatsu called a general’s name and Ieyasu rewarded him, the man would instantly forget the suffering of having narrowly escaped death upon the battlefield.

units.source_en: Tadakatsu was perhaps the elder of the Tokugawa house who best understood the ways of the human heart.

paragraphs.source_en: “Masanori. You all fought with astonishing valor today, but you above all left even Ieyasu speechless with wonder.” Ieyasu exclaimed.

units.source_en: You all fought with astonishing valor today, but you above all left even Ieyasu speechless with wonder.”

paragraphs.source_en: “To take so many lives is a grievous sin indeed.”

units.source_en: “To take so many lives is a grievous sin indeed.”

paragraphs.source_zh: “杀生过多，实在是罪孽啊。”

paragraphs.source_en: “Ieyasu has heard the great name of Gamō Bitchū-no-kami since childhood. It is truly lamentable. See that his head is suitably buried, as you judge proper.”
